interview.hardest_part: Real-time combat with only one 0.5-second input per turn: dodging projectile patterns and contact damage requires fine, reactive movement (small taps, quick direction reversals) that I can't express, so every enemy room and especially bosses chip away health I can't easily replace.
interview.likely_failure: Dying to a floor-3/4/5 boss or a crowded enemy room in the Caves/Depths — either getting cornered with no clean escape step or bleeding out over many small hits — or losing too much wall-clock time to cautious play and never reaching Mom. Bosses with adds and fast projectiles (and Mom's spawn-heavy fight) are the most probable run-enders.
interview.helpful_mechanics: Discrete grid rooms with doors that lock until cleared give clear, stable goals; I can fight from range, kite enemies along room edges, and use diagonal movement plus constant firing to strafe-shoot. Health pickups, bombs, and pedestal items are collected by simply walking over them, the seed is fixed so layouts can be learned across attempts, and the game pauses while I think, so I can plan each step deliberately. Normal difficulty and slow, readable early-floor enemies favour patient, methodical clearing.
interview.harmful_mechanics: Every action commits a full 0.5 s of movement and a fixed fire direction, so I cannot micro-adjust, stop instantly, or dodge reactively; aiming is limited to 4 cardinal directions; contact damage and enemy projectiles punish imprecise positioning; only three starting red hearts with no items means little margin for error; and the 3-hour wall-clock budget including my thinking time constrains how carefully I can afford to play each room.
